name: Ashburn, VA

sources.buildings: OpenStreetMap via Overpass: 15,077 heated buildings within 5 km, 1,367 footprints within 1.2 km for the map, 10 water areas
sources.supply: Lansing supply model (data/supply.csv) scaled to 100 MW IT

notes: Heat demand is ESTIMATED, not metered: OSM footprint x levels (defaults by type when untagged) x heat intensity by building type (residential 110, office 90, school 100, retail 120, restaurant 150, clinic 150, hospital 180, industrial/warehouse 60 kWh/m2.yr at 3,500 HDD (18 C base); assumption - verify), space heat scaled by this location's 2,043 HDD vs 3,500; hourly shape max(0, 16 C - T) + 15% flat hot water; P10/P90 = P50 -/+ 35%.
What buildings pay for heat today is unknown here: design.py uses its default fuel cost.
Prices, grid carbon and cooling constants are the Lansing (upstate NY) defaults; verify locally.
Data-center buildings, garages/sheds and anonymous boxes over 10,000 m2 (likely data halls or warehouses) are excluded from demand.
display_name: Ashburn, Loudoun County, Virginia, United States

first_lines: Reuse 77% of the site's 636 GWh/yr of captured heat (493 GWh/yr), for a combined 20-year NPV of $161.6M and 117,302 t CO2/yr avoided:
1. Trucked thermal storage (PCM containers): 483 of 483 large off-network users pay off. 324.9 GWh/yr, NPV $128.8M.
2. Greenhouse (year-round produce): 22.0 MW peak (40.0 acres), takes 40 C heat directly at the site. 53.8 GWh/yr, NPV $13.3M.
